groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: How's your dissertation going? I'm proofreading my first draft and will submit it to my professor tomorrow.
W: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.
M: You mean you haven't even begun yours yet? The final draft is due in five months.
W: Of course I've started it, but I can't get to the writing yet as I haven't found enough resources to use, so I'm still researching the topic.
M: Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research. I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.
W: I've tried all that, but don't have enough to write the dissertation as my department's minimum length is 70 pages. I think the problem is that my topic isn't viable. And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material. But I was so interested in the topic that I didn't let his advice turn me.
M: Well, I suggest you find a new topic. After all, our professors are here to guide us, so it's best to listen to them.
W: In retrospect, I wish I had listened to him, but I didn't. And now I don't want to give up my topic as I've already invested so much time and energy.
M: If you're committed to your current topic, maybe you could make some adjustments rather than abandon it completely. What is your topic?
W: It's "Depictions of Femininity in Folklore from the South of the Country".
M: That's pretty narrow. You could find more material if you made the topic broader, maybe by including other kinds of depictions.
W: Broadening the topic is a great idea, I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: Today, on Book Talk, we are lucky enough to host John Robbins and discuss his new book, Why Americans Are Fat and How We Can Lose Weight. John isn't just a respected writer; he's also one of the rare celebrity authors writing about science today.
M: Thanks for having me, Rebecca, but I'm hardly a celebrity.
W: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages. What makes people so fascinated with your work?
M: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese. And other countries are facing similar problems. Basically, we all want to know how to fix things.
W: We certainly do. I've read your new book, and it's fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand. That's no small achievement.
M: I'm glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried when I wrote it that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience. My last book was written primarily for the medical community. But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight.
W: And how do you suggest they do that? Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight?
M: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs. I don't advocate one single diet. Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others. And different people need different amounts of protein and fat.
W: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating ten servings of vegetables and three of fruit a day. We'll talk about those recommendations next, but now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Stress is often depicted as negative, but research shows that moderate amounts of it can be beneficial for your brain and your body.
First, the benefits for the brain. Studies have shown that short periods of stress can actually bolster cognitive functioning. Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells. The rats also did better on a memory test later on. Scientists think the same thing happens in humans. But how does stress improve memory? It's simple. When your brain cells multiply, your memory can improve. Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense, because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future. If an animal encounters a predator and escapes, for example, it's important to remember where and when that encounter happened. Experts assert that the same principle applies to humans.
Now, let's turn to how stress benefits the body. This may come as a surprise to laymen. But experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick. Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness. But research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning. One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness. For humans, there's even evidence that experiencing stress before getting vaccinated could help make vaccines more effective.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
For many managers and people who work in leadership positions, dealing with emails is a dilemma. It's likely the "unpredictable, uncontrollable and ongoing nature of day-to-day email in terms of volume, importance and urgency" contributes to their levels of anxiety and to diminished leadership skills.
That's because it's not unusual for many leaders to prioritize email management over people management. An obsession with managing their inbox prevents them from dealing with their employees. As a result, they ignore the issues that might only be mild problems at first, until unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis by virtue of neglect.
As leaders, they are expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer-term strategic goals and also, less ambitiously but more practically, to monitor their daily output, to set clear expectations and to give regular feedback.
When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter. Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress. This is because leaders must divert resources from other tasks to check, filter and respond to emails.
The solution is cultivating self-control which is like a muscle—it can be strengthened or improved over time through exercise. Some suggestions include making space in your diary for the only periods during which you'll be checking emails, setting a timer for yourself so you don't become distracted by your inbox for too long, turning off email alerts so you're not interrupted by them.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
In last week's lecture, we talked about the problems caused by poor eating habits, focusing on how medical professionals are trying to solve these problems. Today, we'll continue with the topic, but focus on research from a different field—marketing.
Now, what can marketing tell us about improving nutrition? Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices.
Those marketing experts assert that the impact of the appearance of food is greater than we might presume, and might hold the key to encouraging better eating. So how important is the appearance of food?
Research shows that just seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement, for example, can cause individuals to imagine the taste or smell of that hamburger. This can make them more likely to purchase and consume it. Of course, that's the point of advertisements. So isn't that a good thing?
Well, the marketing professors argue that this is actually a problem, because the combination of pleasing aesthetics of and easy access to unhealthy foods, such as hamburgers and pizza, may be contributing to a worldwide health crisis. In fact, statistics show that 39% of all adults in the world weigh too much and another 13% are obese.
Now, as we discussed last time, medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar and calorie content. But they've had limited success.
The marketing professors believe that the real solution to obesity is making food look appealing and focusing on the pleasure of both looking at and eating that food. That pleasure can be used as a tool to promote healthy food choices. In fact, the research done by the team showed that associating healthy food with pleasant images, experiences and emotions led to greater interest in purchasing or eating it. "This is a better strategy," they claim, than reminding consumers that a certain food is good for them. But are they right?
Well, the researchers cited a marketing campaign designed to reverse the sales decline of carrots. The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities, but embraced their beauty and the pleasure derived from eating them. For example, the ads focused on the bright, beautiful orange color and crisp texture of the carrots. The campaign led to an impressive increase in product sales of more than 10%. The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
The household cleaning products industry really began to take off in the 1950s. Prior to that, resourceful housewives who had grown up in a less prosperous era relied on substances that they used in their kitchens such as vinegar used to clean windows.
Today, the household cleaning products industry is worth billions of dollars a year and is dominated by large global companies. In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products, and they're doing good business too.
One reason for this is that consumers are becoming more aware of environment and sustainability issues. They also want to make their home a safe place, free from toxic chemicals. The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater. In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible.
There is perhaps no better example of this than a patented cloth sold by one company, which remarkably uses only water rather than traditional cleaning products. The company claims its cloth lifts, traps and removes dirt and bacteria. And considering that people don't see these products in shops, or advertised on TV or in the press, it has been a pretty steep rise.
Many of the people behind these companies began testing the viability of their products by selling them at local markets. Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues. There are also TV shows and books dedicated to maintaining home tidiness and cleanliness and the benefits of having a clean home.
Having a safe and clean home might be one thing people feel they can control in an increasingly out-of-control world. And there are social media celebrities. One woman in Britain has become a social media sensation with more than two million followers for her cleaning tips page.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual: throw a penny into the water, and your wish might come true. But all that money has to go somewhere. Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountains' works. Today, I'm going to talk about where all the coins go.
Well, the coins collected can go to all sorts of different places—from fountain maintenance to charity or public service. In New York City, for example, coins collected from fountains in public parks often go towards the fountains' maintenance itself, though entrepreneurs who don't mind getting their hands wet often get to it first. There are over 50 beautiful decorative display fountains in New York City parks. They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks. But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.
Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul. Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain: for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return. So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day. Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy. And collecting that cash is serious business. Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain. In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them. Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.
For the most part, money collected from privately-owned fountains in the United States also goes to charity. The fountain in New York City's Bryant Park is owned and operated by a not-for-profit corporation, which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance. Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children living in the state. Whether or not your wish comes true after tossing a coin into a fountain, you can rest assured knowing that the change is likely going to someone who needs it.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her dissertation?
options: She hasn't started writing it.
She hasn't decided on a topic.
She is proofreading the first draft.
She is working on the references.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about her dissertation? 

 【翻译】 女士对她的论文说了什么? 
 A)  她还没有开始写。 
 B)  她还没有确定题目。 
 C)  她正在校对初稿。 
 D)  她正在整理参考文献。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） She hasn't started writing it. 
 【定位】 P2 W: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester. 
 女：哦，我连写都还没开始呢，所以我真的很担心能不能在下学期末之前完成。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答 。男生先问 How's your dissertation going，女生张口第一句 I haven't even started writing mine yet 就是对提问的直接应答，对话题的答案就落在被问者这第一反应上。 

 【替换】 I haven't even started writing mine yet ↔ She hasn't started writing it. 去掉 even 的同义压缩 

 【排除】 B) 偷换概念 She hasn't decided on a topic. 听着也像『没进展』，但女生说的是还没开始写，topic 在后文 I'm still researching the topic 里指『还在查资料』，并非『没定下题目』，属偷换概念。  借用原文：I'm still researching the topic 

 C) 张冠李戴 She is proofreading the first draft. 里 proofreading the first draft 确在录音中出现，但说这话的是男生 I'm proofreading my first draft，不是女生，张冠李戴。  借用原文：I'm proofreading my first draft 

 D) 未提及 She is working on the references. 说她在弄参考文献，意味着正文已近完成，与她『还没动笔』完全矛盾，录音里也没说她在做文献，属未提及。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about his professor?
options: He lent many books to the man for reference.
He offered the man advice on resource hunting
He published a lot in a number of reputable journals.
He told the man to be selective when using e-resources.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about his professor? 

 【翻译】 男士对他的教授说了什么? 
 A)  他借给男士许多书供参考。 
 B)  他就资源搜寻向男士提供了建议。 
 C)  他在多个知名期刊上发表了大量文章。 
 D)  他告诉男士在使用电子资源时要有选择性。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） He offered the man advice on resource hunting 
 【定位】 P5 M: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet. 
 男：我一开始是去找我教授聊该上哪儿找资料，在这个基础上，我在图书馆找到了书，还在网上找到很多有声望的期刊文章。 

 【信号】 经过句里的求助动作 。男生回顾自己怎么做研究，关键在 I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information——他教授给的正是『去哪找资料』的指点，这句叙述里藏着教授的作为。 

 【替换】 talking to my professor about where to look for information ↔ He offered the man advice on resource hunting 把『聊去哪找资料』概括为『给找资料建议』 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 He lent many books to the man for reference. 里 books 确在录音出现，但 I found books in the library 是男生自己在图书馆找到的书，不是教授借给他的，原词陷阱。  借用原文：I found books in the library 

 C) 原词陷阱 He published a lot in a number of reputable journals. 用了原词 reputable journal，但 a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet 说的是男生在网上找到这些文章来读，而非教授在期刊上发表论文，原词陷阱兼无中生有。  借用原文：a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet 

 D) 未提及 He told the man to be selective when using e-resources. 说教授叮嘱『用电子资源要有选择』，但录音里教授只指点了去哪找，从未提『要挑着用』，selective 是未提及。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her professor?
options: He didn't think her dissertation topic viable.
He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic.
He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation.
He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about her professor? 

 【翻译】 女士对她的教授说了什么? 
 A)  他认为她的论文题目不可行。 
 B)  他对她的论文题目不感兴趣。 
 C)  他不希望她仓促完成论文。 
 D)  他没有具体说明她的论文篇幅。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） He didn't think her dissertation topic viable. 
 【定位】 P6 W: And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material. 
 女：说实话，我教授一开始就警告过我，我可能找不到足够的材料。 

 【信号】 引述动词 warn 引出原话 。女生用 my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material 转述教授当初的警告，引述动词 warn 后面那句就是教授的态度，是答案句。 

 【替换】 warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material ↔ He didn't think her dissertation topic viable. 『找不到材料』即『选题不可行』 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic. 把 interested 安在教授身上，但录音里 I was so interested in the topic 说有兴趣的是女生自己，教授只是警告找不到料，张冠李戴又偷换。  借用原文：I was so interested in the topic 

 C) 未提及 He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation. 说教授不想她赶工，但教授只警告材料不够，从没说过快慢、赶不赶的事，未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation. 提到 length，录音里 length 出现在 my department's minimum length is 70 pages，那是系里的规定，与教授说没说清篇幅无关，原词陷阱。  借用原文：my department's minimum length is 70 pages

questions.prompt: What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation?
options: Change her research methodology.
Narrow down her dissertation topic.
Consult her professor more.
Follow the man's advice.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation? 

 【翻译】 我们了解到女士将做什么来完成她的论文? 
 A)  改变她的研究方法。 
 B)  缩小她的论文题目范围。 
 C)  多咨询她的教授。 
 D)  听从男士的建议。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Follow the man's advice. 
 【定位】 P12 W: Broadening the topic is a great idea, I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country. 
 女：把题目扩大是个好主意，我打算先把全国其他地区的民间传说也纳进来。 

 【信号】 结尾采纳建议的应答 。男生上一句建议 You could find more material if you made the topic broader，女生末句 Broadening the topic is a great idea 当即采纳，结尾这句『接受建议』就是答案句。 

 【替换】 Broadening the topic is a great idea ↔ Follow the man's advice. 采纳男生提议=照他建议办 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Change her research methodology. 沾了男生那句 Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research，但女生最终决定的是扩大题目，并没说要换研究方法，原词陷阱。  借用原文：Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research 

 B) 与原文相反 Narrow down her dissertation topic. 与女生的决定正好相反——男生说题目 That's pretty narrow，建议 made the topic broader，女生要做的是 broaden（扩大）而非 narrow（缩小），与原文相反。  借用原文：That's pretty narrow 

 C) 原词陷阱 Consult her professor more. 里 professor 全程反复出现，诱人选；但女生采纳的是男生当下的建议，并未表示要再去多问教授，原词陷阱。  借用原文：our professors are here to guide us

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the man in her introduction?
options: He has translated 12 books.
He is a well-known nutritionist.
His books sell well worldwide.
His latest book sold a million copies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about the man in her introduction? 

 【翻译】 女士在介绍中是如何评价这位男士的? 
 A)  他已经翻译了12本书。 
 B)  他是一位知名的营养学家。 
 C)  他的书在全球销量很好。 
 D)  他的最新著作售出了一百万册。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） His books sell well worldwide. 
 【定位】 P3 That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages. 
 您这么说太谦虚了，毕竟您的四本书在全球总共卖出了七百万册，还被翻译成了 12 种不同的语言。 

 【信号】 主持人介绍嘉宾的成就陈述句 。答案信号是主持人介绍环节里铺陈嘉宾业绩的那句 your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide——访谈开场的 "夸业绩" 句往往就是 introduction 题的答案句。 

 【替换】 sold a total of seven million copies worldwide ↔ His books sell well worldwide "全球卖出七百万册" 概括为 "全球畅销" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音说 translated into 12 different languages(译成 12 种语言)，A 却说 He has translated 12 books.(翻译了 12 本书)——盗用了原文数字 12，却把对象从 "语言" 换成 "书"，且作者是 "被翻译" 不是 "去翻译"，听到 12 就选必中招。  借用原文：translated into 12 different languages 

 B) 未提及 录音介绍他是 a respected writer 和写科学的 celebrity authors，从没说他是 a well-known nutritionist.(知名营养师)。营养师是顺着 "减肥饮食" 话题脑补出来的，原文未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 录音是 your four books have sold a total of seven million copies(四本书合计七百万册)，D 说 His latest book sold a million copies.(最新一本卖了一百万册)——盗用 "百万册级销量" 的语感，却把 "四本合计七百万" 偷换成 "单本一百万"，数字与范围全错。  借用原文：your four books have sold a total of seven million copies

questions.prompt: What has motivated the man to write his books?
options: The desire of Americans to try exotic cuisines.
The demand for information about food safety.
The fact that over half of Americans are overweight.
The fact that science books are difficult to read.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has motivated the man to write his books? 

 【翻译】 是什么促使这位男士写作这些书? 
 A)  美国人尝试异国风味美食的渴望。 
 B)  对食品安全信息的需求。 
 C)  超过半数美国人超重的事实。 
 D)  科学书籍难以阅读的事实。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The fact that over half of Americans are overweight. 
 【定位】 P4 Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese. 
 嗯，人们读我的书，是因为超过 60% 的美国人超重，甚至肥胖。 

 【信号】 因果连接词 because 引出原因 。答案信号是显性因果词 because：people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight，because 后面那句现象即为写书/读书的动机。 

 【替换】 more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese ↔ The fact that over half of Americans are overweight "超 60%" 等价于 "过半" 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 The desire of Americans to try exotic cuisines.(想尝异国菜)在整段对话里没有任何对应，纯属话题跑偏的捏造，与减肥饮食主线无关。 
 B) 未提及 The demand for information about food safety.(对食品安全信息的需求)听上去与饮食沾边，但录音给的动机是 "超重"，从未谈 food safety，属顺着话题脑补的未提及项。 
 D) 与原文相反 录音里 "科学难懂" 是被作者 make difficult science easy for laymen to understand 克服的难点、是卖点，而非写书动机；D 却把 science books are difficult to read. 说成动机，盗用了 "difficult science" 的字眼却把作用讲反了。  借用原文：make difficult science easy for laymen to understand

questions.prompt: Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for?
options: The general public.
Those who are overweight.
Those who want to lose weight.

questions.explanation:
【题目】 Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for? 

 【翻译】 这位男士说他的上一本书主要是为谁而写的? 
 A)  普通大众。 
 B)  超重人群。 
 C)  想要减肥的人。 
 D)  医学界。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The medical community. 
 【定位】 P6 My last book was written primarily for the medical community. But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight. 
 我上一本书主要是为医学界写的。但这一次，我想帮助普通人掌控自己的体重。 

 【信号】 限定词 last + 受众句，并与 "this time" 对照 。答案信号是 My last book was written primarily for the medical community 这句明确的 "上一本 written for 谁"，紧接的 But this time 形成 "上一本 vs 这一本" 对照，提醒要选 last 对应的那一群。 

 【替换】 My last book was written primarily for the medical community ↔ The medical community 受众原词直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 The general public. 对应的是 this time, I want to help ordinary people——那是 "这一本(新书)" 的受众。把 this time 的受众安到 last book 头上，正是没分清两本书的张冠李戴。  借用原文：this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight 

 B) 原词陷阱 Those who are overweight. 借了通篇出现的 overweight 一词，但录音从没说哪本书是 "为超重者" 而写；它只是话题词，不是 last book 的受众。  借用原文：more than 60% of Americans are overweight 

 C) 答非所问 Those who want to lose weight. 贴合全场减肥主题、最顺耳，但录音说 last book 是写给 medical community 的；"想减肥的人" 从未被点名为某本书的受众，是借主题诱选。
questions.spoken_text: Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for?

questions.prompt: What does the man recommend people do?
options: Switch to a vegetarian diet.
Follow a personalized diet.
Adhere to doctors' advice.
Cut carbohydrate intake.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man recommend people do? 

 【翻译】 这位男士建议人们做什么? 
 A)  改吃素食。 
 B)  遵循个性化饮食方案。 
 C)  听从医生的建议。 
 D)  减少碳水化合物摄入。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Follow a personalized diet. 
 【定位】 P8 Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs. I don't advocate one single diet. 
 简单说，我主张每个人都要考虑自己的新陈代谢，吃适合自己身体需求的东西。我不提倡某一种单一的食谱。 

 【信号】 主张句 I argue + 否定 I don't advocate 立反差 。答案信号是主张句 I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs，再以 I don't advocate one single diet 否定 "单一食谱"——一立一否，强调的正是 "因人而异"。 

 【替换】 every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs ↔ Follow a personalized diet "按各自身体需求吃" 概括为 "个性化饮食" 
 I don't advocate one single diet ↔ Follow a personalized diet "不主张单一食谱" 反面印证 "个性化" 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Switch to a vegetarian diet.(改吃素)在对话里没有依据；录音末尾虽提到多吃蔬果，但那是补充建议，从没让人 "改成素食"，属未提及的绝对化主张。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Adhere to doctors' advice. 借了前文 the medical community 留下的 "医学" 印象，但作者建议的是按自身代谢来，从没让普通人 "遵医嘱"，是盗用医学语感的诱选。  借用原文：My last book was written primarily for the medical community 

 D) 与原文相反 录音说 Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others(有些人该比别人多吃碳水)，是 "碳水因人而异"；D 却笼统说 Cut carbohydrate intake.(减少碳水)，盗用 carbohydrate 一词，却把 "看人而定" 讲成了 "一律削减"，方向相反。  借用原文：Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others
questions.spoken_text: What does the man recommend people do?

questions.prompt: What did researchers discover about rats placed briefly in a stressful situation?
options: The rate of their growth increased dramatically.
The growth of their new brain cells doubled.
They began to show signs of depression.
They began to get irritated and restless.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did researchers discover about rats placed briefly in a stressful situation? 

 【翻译】 研究人员发现,短暂置于压力情境中的大鼠会出现什么情况? 
 A)  它们的生长速度显著加快。 
 B)  它们新生脑细胞的增长翻了一番。 
 C)  它们开始表现出抑郁的迹象。 
 D)  它们开始变得烦躁不安。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） The growth of their new brain cells doubled. 
 【定位】 P2 Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells. 
 研究者发现，把大鼠置于压力情境中仅仅几个小时，就使其新脑细胞的生长翻了一倍。 

 【信号】 discovered 后接发现内容 。答案句由 Researchers discovered that 引出，研究动词 discovered 后面紧跟的就是题干要的发现，是天然的答案信号；同时 doubled the growth of new brain cells 给出明确的量化结果，更确认这就是落点。 

 【替换】 doubled the growth of new brain cells ↔ The growth of their new brain cells doubled. 主被动语序调换 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 A 说 rate of their growth increased dramatically（成长速率剧增），但录音说的是生长翻倍（数量翻番），讲的是结果量而非速率；它盗用了原文 growth 一词，却把翻倍偷换成速率剧增，答非所问。  借用原文：doubled the growth of new brain cells 

 C) 未提及 C 说大鼠出现 signs of depression（抑郁迹象），但录音通篇讲的是适度压力的好处，从未提大鼠抑郁，属于无中生有。 
 D) 未提及 D 说大鼠变得 irritated and restless（烦躁不安），录音只说短暂压力让脑细胞翻倍、记忆变好，没说大鼠情绪烦躁，是凭压力等于负面的常识硬加的，未提及。
questions.spoken_text: What did researchers discover about rats, placed briefly in a stressful situation?

questions.prompt: Why do people tend to have clear memories of dangerous situations they have encountered?
options: To avoid them in the future.
To warn others against them.
To make good sense of them.
To reflect on their causes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do people tend to have clear memories of dangerous situations they have encountered? 

 【翻译】 为什么人们往往对自己遭遇的危险情境有清晰的记忆? 
 A)  为了在将来避免这些情境。 
 B)  为了警告他人不要遭遇这些情境。 
 C)  为了合理理解这些情境。 
 D)  为了反思这些情境的起因。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） To avoid them in the future. 
 【定位】 P2 Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense, because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future. 
 从生物学角度看，这是有道理的，因为更善于记住危险情境的动物能在将来躲开它们。 

 【信号】 because 引出真原因 。答案句的核心信号是 because，题干问 Why，录音里紧跟 because 后的 can avoid them in the future 正是要的原因——因果连词后面就是答案落点。 

 【替换】 can avoid them in the future ↔ To avoid them in the future. 几乎原义照搬 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 B 说为了 warn others against them（警告别人提防），录音只说记住是为了自己将来躲开，从未提及把危险告诉他人，属未提及。 
 C) 未提及 C 说为了 make good sense of them（弄懂它们），录音讲的目的是 avoid（躲开）而非理解其含义，方向不符，原文无此说法。 
 D) 未提及 D 说为了 reflect on their causes（反思其成因），录音从没提反思危险的起因，只说记住以便将来躲开，是凭常识硬推的目的，未提及。
questions.spoken_text: Why do people tend to have clearer memories of dangerous situations they have encountered?

questions.prompt: What do scientists believe chronic stress can do?
options: Produce a surprising healing effect.
Weaken one's immunity in the long run.
Make people more susceptible to illness.
Provide protection against mental illnesses.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do scientists believe chronic stress can do? 

 【翻译】 科学家认为慢性压力会造成什么影响? 
 A)  产生令人惊讶的疗愈效果。 
 B)  从长远来看削弱人的免疫力。 
 C)  使人更容易生病。 
 D)  提供针对精神疾病的保护。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Make people more susceptible to illness. 
 【定位】 P3 Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness. 
 科学家承认，长期压力会让你更容易生病。 

 【信号】 concede 后的让步内容 。答案句出现题干关键词 chronic stress，并由 Scientists concede that 引出科学家的让步看法；问 chronic 就只认带 chronic 的这句，其后的 make you more prone to illness 即答案。 

 【替换】 make you more prone to illness ↔ Make people more susceptible to illness. 近义词替换 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 A 说产生 surprising healing effect（惊人疗愈效果），录音里令人意外的好处是说短期压力 provide some protection against getting sick，而题干问的是 chronic（长期）；A 张冠李戴，把短期压力的好处安到了长期压力头上。  借用原文：short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick 

 B) 与原文相反 B 说 Weaken one's immunity in the long run（长期削弱免疫力），录音讲免疫只说短期压力 increases your immune functioning（增强免疫），从没说长期压力削弱免疫；B 反了方向又借用 long run 来唬人。  借用原文：increases your immune functioning 

 D) 偷换概念 D 说 protection against mental illnesses（防护精神疾病），录音说的是短期压力 provide some protection against getting sick（防普通生病），既错把长期当短期，又把笼统的生病偷换成 mental illnesses（精神疾病）。  借用原文：provide some protection against getting sick
questions.spoken_text: What do scientists believe chronic stress can do?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is a common problem with managers?
options: Placing their own interests over their staff's.
Being overwhelmed by their daily routines.
Lacking the ability to relate to their staff.
Spending too much time handling email.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say is a common problem with managers? 

 【翻译】 说话者认为管理者常见的问题是什么? 
 A)  将自己的利益置于员工之上。 
 B)  被日常事务压得喘不过气来。 
 C)  缺乏与员工建立联系的能力。 
 D)  花费太多时间处理电子邮件。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Spending too much time handling email. 
 【定位】 P4 When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter. Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress. 
 当要在收件箱的诱惑与其他更重要的事务之间做选择时，许多人牺牲了后者（更重要的事）。每天的邮件需求对他们的目标推进产生了负面影响。 

 【信号】 概括管理者通病的陈述句 。这句不是靠某个转折词跳出来，而是全篇反复落到同一点：管理者把精力压在邮箱上而牺牲更重要的事。many sacrifice the latter 与 prioritize email management over people management 互相印证，共同指向"花太多时间在邮件上"这个通病。 

 【替换】 Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress ↔ Spending too much time handling email "邮件占用精力"换说成"花太多时间处理邮件" 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 录音说的是管理者把邮件管理置于人员管理之上 prioritize email management over people management，置于上面的是"邮件"而非"自身利益"；A 把 over...staff 的句式留下，却换成 own interests，是偷换。  借用原文：prioritize email management over people management 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音强调的是被"邮件"困住，未说被泛泛的"日常事务（daily routines）"压垮；B 借了 day-to-day 的感觉 day-to-day email，却把焦点从"邮件"扩大成"日常琐事"，范围被放大。  借用原文：day-to-day email 

 C) 过度推断 录音只说管理者沉迷邮箱、忽视员工 prevents them from dealing with their employees，是"没空管"，并未说他们"缺乏与员工共情的能力（relate to staff）"；从"没空管"推到"没能力"是多走了一步。  借用原文：prevents them from dealing with their employees
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker say is a common problem with managers?

questions.prompt: What may happen when managers ignore minor problems?
options: Their leadership may be challenged.
Their companies may go bankrupt.
Unexpected events may occur.
Major problems may result.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What may happen when managers ignore minor problems? 

 【翻译】 当管理者忽视小问题时可能会发生什么? 
 A)  他们的领导力可能会受到挑战。 
 B)  他们的公司可能会破产。 
 C)  可能会出现意外事件。 
 D)  可能会导致重大问题。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Major problems may result. 
 【定位】 P2 As a result, they ignore the issues that might only be mild problems at first, until unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis by virtue of neglect. 
 结果，他们忽视了那些起初可能只是轻微问题的事，直到这些问题不幸地、不可避免地因疏忽而演变成重大问题或危机。 

 【信号】 until 之后才是结果落点 。因果信号在 until unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis：起初只是 mild problems，until 之后才转成 major problem。听这类题不能停在"小问题"那半句，落点在 until / transform into 之后的结果。 

 【替换】 transform into a major problem or crisis ↔ Major problems may result "演变成重大问题"="重大问题随之产生" 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 录音前文确实提到 leadership skills 会下降 diminished leadership skills，但那是讲邮件焦虑的背景，不是"忽视小问题"这一动作的后果；A 把别处出现的 leadership 搬来当本题结果，张冠李戴。  借用原文：diminished leadership skills 

 B) 过度推断 录音最重只说到 major problem or crisis（重大问题或危机），并未说严重到"公司破产"；B 把"危机"夸大为"破产"，超出录音程度。 
 C) 与原文相反 录音用 inevitably transform（不可避免地演变）强调这是必然结果，而 C 说"unexpected events（意外事件）"，恰与"不可避免"相反。  借用原文：they inevitably transform
questions.spoken_text: What may happen when managers ignore minor problems?

questions.prompt: What are leaders expected to do in pursuing their strategic goals?
options: Keep an eye on their employees.
Motivate and inspire their team.
Sacrifice some of the immediate goals.
Have greater ambition in overall planning.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are leaders expected to do in pursuing their strategic goals? 

 【翻译】 领导者在追求战略目标时应该做什么? 
 A)  密切关注他们的员工。 
 B)  激励和鼓舞他们的团队。 
 C)  牺牲一些眼前目标。 
 D)  在整体规划中具有更大的雄心。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Motivate and inspire their team. 
 【定位】 P3 As leaders, they are expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer-term strategic goals and also, less ambitiously but more practically, to monitor their daily output, to set clear expectations and to give regular feedback. 
 作为领导者，他们被期望去激励和鼓舞团队以追求更长远的战略目标，同时，作为志向稍低但更务实的一面，去监督日常产出、设定明确预期并给予定期反馈。 

 【信号】 are expected to + 限定语 in pursuit of strategic goals 。信号是 expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer-term strategic goals：be expected to 直接给出"被期望做的事"，而题干限定"追求战略目标时"，正好对应 in pursuit of...strategic goals 这一半，落点就在 motivate and inspire。 

 【替换】 motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer-term strategic goals ↔ Motivate and inspire their team 原句动作原样保留 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 录音里"监督"出现在 to monitor their daily output，这属于后半句"志向稍低、更务实"的日常事务，而非题干所问的"追求战略目标"那部分；A 借 monitor 的意思，却挂错了半句。  借用原文：to monitor their daily output 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音 P4 说的是管理者"牺牲更重要的事" many sacrifice the latter，并不是"牺牲眼前目标"，且那是讲管理者的毛病、不是"被期望做的事"；C 把 sacrifice 一词搬来制造熟悉感。  借用原文：many sacrifice the latter 

 D) 过度推断 录音只说战略目标是 longer-term（更长远）longer-term strategic goals，并未要求领导"在整体规划上更有野心"；D 把"长远"擅自升级成"更大野心的规划"。  借用原文：longer-term strategic goals
questions.spoken_text: What are leaders expected to do in pursuing their strategic goals?

questions.prompt: How can a manager best avoid being distracted by email?
options: Cultivate self-control.
Filter their email boxes.
Respond only after work.
Check only when necessary.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How can a manager best avoid being distracted by email? 

 【翻译】 管理者如何才能最好地避免被电子邮件分散注意力? 
 A)  培养自我控制能力。 
 B)  过滤他们的电子邮件收件箱。 
 C)  仅在下班后回复。 
 D)  仅在必要时查看。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Cultivate self-control. 
 【定位】 P5 The solution is cultivating self-control which is like a muscle—it can be strengthened or improved over time through exercise. 
 解决办法是培养自控力，它就像一块肌肉——可以通过锻炼随时间不断增强或提升。 

 【信号】 The solution is 给总方案 。信号是 The solution is cultivating self-control：The solution is 直接抛出总的解决办法。题干带 best，要的正是这条根本方案，而其后的 making space in your diary、setting a timer 等都只是它名下的"具体小做法"，不是总解。 

 【替换】 The solution is cultivating self-control ↔ Cultivate self-control 总方案原样对应 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到 check, filter and respond to emails 里有 filter，但那是描述邮件耗费精力，不是给的解决建议；filter 一词制造了熟悉感，却答非"best 的总办法"。  借用原文：check, filter and respond to emails 

 C) 未提及 录音的具体建议是"在日程里划出专门查邮件的时段" making space in your diary for the only periods during which you'll be checking emails，并没有说"只在下班后回复"；C 是凭常识臆造的做法。 
 D) 答非所问 录音建议是"划定专门时段查"与"设定时器" setting a timer for yourself so you don't become distracted，更接近 D 的味道，但 D 仍只是 self-control 名下的具体操作；题干带 best，要的是总方案 A 而非这条小招。  借用原文：making space in your diary for the only periods during which you'll be checking emails
questions.spoken_text: How can a manager best avoid being distracted by email?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say a team of marketing professors has studied?
options: The key to increasing healthy food supply.
The best way to improve marketing research.
The impact of advertisements on consumption.
The importance of the appearance of food.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say a team of marketing professors has studied? 

 【翻译】 说话者说一个营销学教授团队研究了什么? 
 A)  增加健康食品供应的关键。 
 B)  改进营销研究的最佳方法。 
 C)  广告对消费的影响。 
 D)  食物外观的重要性。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The importance of the appearance of food. 
 【定位】 P2 Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices. 
 嗯，一组营销学教授研究了食物视觉方面的重要性，以及它如何影响食物选择。 

 【信号】 题干原词 studied 在原文直接出现 。录音 a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food 与题干同用 studied，是对研究对象的直接交代，定位信号明确，无需转折或推断。 

 【替换】 the importance of the visual aspect of food ↔ The importance of the appearance of food. visual aspect 同义改写为 appearance 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项把录音多次提到的 healthy 拼成 increasing healthy food supply，但录音研究的是外观对选择的影响，从未谈增加健康食品的供给量，属听到 healthy 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：promote healthy food choices 

 B) 原词陷阱 选项借用录音里的 marketing 拼成 improve marketing research，但讲者说的是营销学者拿来研究外观，而非研究如何改进市场调研本身，属答非所问。  借用原文：a team of marketing professors 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音确实在 seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement 提到广告，但那是用来举例说明外观如何起作用，不是这组学者研究的对象；选项把举例细节当成研究主题，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement

questions.prompt: How have medical professionals tried to fight obesity?
options: By focusing on the nutrients in different foods.
By emphasizing the diversity of food.
By stressing pleasing aesthetics of food.
By winning the support of marketing professors.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How have medical professionals tried to fight obesity? 

 【翻译】 医疗专业人员如何努力对抗肥胖? 
 A)  通过关注不同食物中的营养成分。 
 B)  通过强调食物的多样性。 
 C)  通过强调食物赏心悦目的美感。 
 D)  通过赢得营销学教授的支持。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） By focusing on the nutrients in different foods. 
 【定位】 P6 medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar and calorie content. 
 医学专家曾试图通过关注不同食物中的营养成分来对抗肥胖流行病，强调诸如碳水化合物、脂肪、糖和卡路里含量之类的东西。 

 【信号】 主体词 medical professionals 领出做法句 。录音 medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients 主体与题干完全一致，by focusing on 直接给出做法，是该主体名下的答案句信号。 

 【替换】 by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods ↔ By focusing on the nutrients in different foods. 几乎原句对应仅省略 found 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 选项 By emphasizing the diversity of food. 的 diversity 在录音里从未出现，医学专家强调的是营养成分而非食物多样性，属无中生有。 
 C) 张冠李戴 强调美感 By stressing pleasing aesthetics of food. 确是录音里的做法，但那是营销学者的主张，不是医学专家的做法；选项把营销学者的招安到医学专家头上，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：the combination of pleasing aesthetics 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 By winning the support of marketing professors. 借用录音里的 marketing professors，但录音从没说医学专家去争取营销教授的支持，二者只是讲座中并列对比的两方，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：a team of marketing professors

questions.prompt: What can other companies learn from the example of the carrot promotion campaign?
options: They can attract customers with the healthy qualities of their products.
They can boost sales of healthy foods by making them visually appealing.
They can turn to marketing professors for advice.
They can rely on advertising for sales promotion.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What can other companies learn from the example of the carrot promotion campaign? 

 【翻译】 其他公司能从胡萝卜促销活动的例子中学到什么? 
 A)  它们可以用产品的健康品质吸引顾客。 
 B)  它们可以通过使健康食品在视觉上更吸引人来提升销量。 
 C)  它们可以向营销学教授寻求建议。 
 D)  它们可以依靠广告进行促销。 

 【答案】 B （推断题） They can boost sales of healthy foods by making them visually appealing. 
 【定位】 P8 The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure. 
 研究者认为，其他公司可以用类似的广告来提升健康食品的销量，把它们的产品描绘得有吸引力、是一种愉悦的来源。 

 【信号】 结尾外推句 could+similar 给出启示 。录音结尾 other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads 用 could 与 similar 把胡萝卜案例外推到其他公司，正是题干所问的启示落点。 

 【替换】 bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive ↔ They can boost sales of healthy foods by making them visually appealing. bolster=boost、attractive=visually appealing 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项 They can attract customers with the healthy qualities of their products. 借用录音 didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities 的原词，但录音明说该案例恰恰没强调健康属性，选项把否定说成肯定，属与原文相反。  借用原文：The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 They can turn to marketing professors for advice. 借用录音里的 marketing professors，但讲者说的是公司可用类似广告，从没说让公司去求助营销教授，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：a team of marketing professors 

 D) 偷换概念 选项 They can rely on advertising for sales promotion. 借用录音的 ads，但录音强调的是靠把产品拍得有吸引力、令人愉悦的广告，而非泛泛依赖广告；选项丢掉视觉吸引这一关键限定，属偷换概念。  借用原文：bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years?
options: It has witnessed a spectacular surge in demand.
It has met much criticism from environmentalists.
It has seen more small businesses offering environment-friendly products.
It has experienced increasingly fierce competition among global companies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于近年来清洁产品行业说了什么? 
 A)  该行业需求出现了惊人的激增。 
 B)  该行业受到了环保主义者的诸多批评。 
 C)  该行业出现了更多提供环保产品的小企业。 
 D)  该行业经历了全球公司之间日益激烈的竞争。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It has seen more small businesses offering environment-friendly products. 
 【定位】 P2 In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products, and they're doing good business too. 
 然而近年来，许多国家见证了提供更环保清洁用品的小企业和公司数量激增，而且它们的生意还相当不错。 

 【信号】 时间标志 in recent years + 转折 however 。In recent years, however 同时给出题干要的时间窗和一个转折信号——however 把话锋从前句"大公司主导"转向"小企业崛起"，转折之后才是答案落点。 

 【替换】 a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products ↔ more small businesses offering environment-friendly products a surge in the number of = more 的同义概括 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实念了 surge，但原文是 a surge in the number of small businesses（企业数量激增），选项 a spectacular surge in demand 把它偷换成"需求激增"，听到 surge 就选会中招。  借用原文：a surge in the number of small businesses and companies 

 B) 未提及 选项 much criticism from environmentalists 在录音里找不到任何对应——原文讲的是环保产品走红、生意红火，从无"被批评"之说，属凭空捏造。 
 D) 原词陷阱 录音第2段确有 large global companies，选项 fierce competition among global companies 借这个词造出"全球公司竞争加剧"，可原文只说大公司"主导"行业，没说它们之间竞争更激烈。  借用原文：dominated by large global companies
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years?

questions.prompt: Why are newly developed cleaning products selling well?
options: Consumers now know much more about technology.
Their mass production has sharply reduced the price
Consumers tend to favor all that is novel.
Their quality has been greatly improved.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why are newly developed cleaning products selling well? 

 【翻译】 为什么新开发的清洁产品卖得很好? 
 A)  消费者现在对技术了解得多得多。 
 B)  它们的大规模生产大幅降低了价格。 
 C)  消费者倾向于青睐一切新颖的东西。 
 D)  它们的质量得到了极大改善。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Consumers now know much more about technology. 
 【定位】 P3 The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater. In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible. 
 第三个原因是，人们对技术的认知和了解从未像现在这样深。过去人们可能会怀疑一款号称能达到惊人清洁效果的新产品，但如今他们相信技术有能力做到曾被认为不可能的事。 

 【信号】 明示标志 The third reason + 对应题干"new products" 。The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater 用 The third reason 直接挂出一条理由；题干问的是 newly developed products，对应的正是这条"人们更懂技术、因而信任新产品"的原因。 

 【替换】 people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater ↔ Consumers now know much more about technology knowledge…never been greater = know much more 的同义改写 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 选项 mass production has sharply reduced the price 听上去顺理成章，但录音讲好卖的原因是环保意识、安全、懂技术，从头到尾没提"量产降价"，是用生活常识替代原文。 
 C) 过度推断 选项 favor all that is novel（偏爱一切新奇）看似贴近"新产品"，但录音说的是人们 have faith in technology（信任技术能力），不是"凡新必爱"，把"信任技术"推成"盲目追新"推过了头。  借用原文：they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible 

 D) 偷换概念 选项 quality has been greatly improved 录音并未提及——原文讲的是消费者对技术的"认知与信任"，而非产品"质量本身"提高了，二者不能混为一谈。
questions.spoken_text: Why are newly developed cleaning products selling well?

questions.prompt: What are some customers doing to help promote non-traditional cleaning products?
options: Purchasing only this kind of products for home cleaning.
Writing positive comments about them on social media.
Demonstrating on TV how effective these products are.
Telling one another about their incomparable virtues.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are some customers doing to help promote non-traditional cleaning products? 

 【翻译】 一些顾客正在做什么来帮助推广非传统清洁产品? 
 A)  只购买这类产品用于家庭清洁。 
 B)  在社交媒体上撰写关于它们的正面评论。 
 C)  在电视上演示这些产品有多有效。 
 D)  相互告知它们无可比拟的优点。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Writing positive comments about them on social media. 
 【定位】 P5 Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues. 
 然后，很多情况下，是顾客在为这些产品做营销——他们在社交媒体上留下一串串评论，称赞产品的优点。 

 【信号】 主语对应 customers + 动作 doing the marketing 。customers are doing the marketing for these products 的主语正是题干的 customers、目的正是 help promote（做营销=帮推广），后面 by leaving… 直接交代了具体做法，是答案句。 

 【替换】 leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues ↔ Writing positive comments about them on social media leaving…comments, praising = writing positive comments 的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 Purchasing only this kind of products 里的 only（只买这一种）录音没有任何依据——原文讲顾客帮做营销、写评论，从没说他们"只"用这类产品。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音第4段提过 TV（advertised on TV）、第5段提过 TV shows，选项 Demonstrating on TV 借这些 TV 造"上电视演示"，可原文恰恰说这类产品没在电视宣传、且"上电视演示"是节目而非顾客所为，听到 TV 就选会中招。  借用原文：people don't see these products in shops, or advertised on TV or in the press 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 Telling one another about their incomparable virtues 用了录音的 virtues，但原文顾客是"在社交媒体写评论"称赞，而非 Telling one another（互相口头转告）；盗了对的词、错在渠道。  借用原文：leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues

questions.prompt: What problem might be caused by the growing piles of coins in fountains?
options: Increasing cleaners' workload.
Blocking the fountains' works.
Breaking a time-honored ritual.
Polluting the fountains' water.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What problem might be caused by the growing piles of coins in fountains? 

 【翻译】 喷泉中不断堆积的硬币可能会造成什么问题? 
 A)  增加清洁工的工作量。 
 B)  堵塞喷泉的运作装置。 
 C)  破坏一项由来已久的仪式。 
 D)  污染喷泉的水。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Blocking the fountains' works. 
 【定位】 P1 Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountains' works. 
 否则，越堆越多的便士、25 美分和欧元硬币可能会堵塞喷泉的运作机件。 

 【信号】 Otherwise 引出假设后果 。信号是 Otherwise（否则）——它引出"如果钱不被运走会怎样"的假设性后果，正对题干问的"会造成什么问题"，紧跟其后的 could clog up the fountains' works 就是答案句的核心。 

 【替换】 clog up the fountains' works ↔ Blocking the fountains' works clog up = Blocking 同义替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Increasing cleaners' workload 里的 cleaners 在后文确实反复出现（喷泉由 staff 清理），但录音从没说"硬币堆积会加重清洁工负担"，是借后文的"清洁"话题诱你听到 cleaners 就选。  借用原文：They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks. 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 Breaking a time-honored ritual 直接搬了录音第一句的 time-honored ritual，但那句是说"投币许愿是个老传统"，是引入话题，根本不是在讲"硬币堆积造成的问题"——典型的把开头原词拿来骗。  借用原文：Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual 

 D) 未提及 选项 Polluting the fountains' water 听起来"硬币泡水里好像会污染"很合常识，但录音通篇没提水质污染，是用生活常识替文本作答的典型坑。
questions.spoken_text: What problem might be caused by the growing piles of coins in fountains?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the coins collected from New York City's park fountains?
options: They are occasionally retrieved by curious tourists.
They are regularly donated to charity organizations.
They are mostly used for the fountains' maintenance.
They are usually used as wages for fountain cleaners.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about the coins collected from New York City's park fountains? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于从纽约市公园喷泉中收集的硬币说了什么? 
 A)  它们偶尔会被好奇的游客取走。 
 B)  它们定期捐赠给慈善组织。 
 C)  它们大多用于喷泉的维护。 
 D)  它们通常用作喷泉清洁工的工资。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They are mostly used for the fountains' maintenance. 
 【定位】 P2 But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected. 
 但大部分硬币已经被有生意头脑的纽约人捞走了，剩下能被收走的已所剩无几。 

 【信号】 转折 But 后才是真意 。信号是 But——前半句说"市政人员每几周清理一次"是表面信息，转折 But 之后的 most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers 才是录音真正想强调的实情，这正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 go towards the fountains' maintenance itself ↔ used for the fountains' maintenance go towards=used for 同指用途 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 选项 occasionally retrieved by curious tourists 看似对上"硬币被人提前取走"，但录音说取走硬币的是 entrepreneurial New Yorkers（有生意头脑的纽约人），不是 curious tourists（好奇游客）——把取走者的身份偷换了，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers 

 B) 张冠李戴 选项 donated to charity organizations 里的 charity 录音确有（罗马的钱办惠民超市、迪士尼捐寄养儿童），但那是罗马和迪士尼喷泉的事，不是本题问的纽约公园喷泉——张冠李戴。  借用原文：Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children 

 D) 未提及 选项 used as wages for fountain cleaners 里 cleaners / staff 录音确有（喷泉由公园 staff 清理），但录音从没说硬币被"当作清洁工的工资"，是借"清洁"话题拼出的无中生有。  借用原文：They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the money collected from Rome's Trevi Fountain?
options: It is invested in a series of businesses.
It is used exclusively for its maintenance.
It is used to run a supermarket for the needy.
It is estimated to be about $40,000 a month.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the money collected from Rome's Trevi Fountain? 

 【翻译】 关于从罗马许愿池收集的钱,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它被投资于一系列生意。 
 B)  它专门用于该喷泉的维护。 
 C)  它被用来经营一家为贫困者服务的超市。 
 D)  它估计每月约为40000美元。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It is used to run a supermarket for the needy. 
 【定位】 P3 Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy. 
 每晚收上来的钱，大部分用于运营一家面向困难群体的超市。 

 【信号】 goes towards 点明用途 。信号是表用途的 goes towards（用于……）——它直接交代这笔钱的去向，紧跟其后的 running a supermarket for the needy 就是答案。听到 goes towards 这类"用于"的短语就锁定其后内容。 

 【替换】 running a supermarket for the needy ↔ run a supermarket for the needy running→run 仅词形微调 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 invested in a series of businesses 里 business(es) 一词录音确有（serious business 指"收钱是件正经事"），但那是形容"这事很严肃"，根本不是说钱拿去"投资做生意"——盗用 business 一词制造误会。  借用原文：collecting that cash is serious business 

 B) 张冠李戴 选项 used exclusively for its maintenance 描述的"专门用于喷泉维护"是录音里纽约公园喷泉和 Bryant Park 喷泉的处置，不是罗马许愿池的，张冠李戴；且 exclusively（专门、唯一）程度过死，罗马的钱是"大部分"办超市。  借用原文：which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance 

 D) 与原文相反 选项 about $40,000 a month 把数字改了：录音说的是 as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day（每天约 4000 美元），选项改成"每月 4 万"——金额和时间单位都被动了手脚，是典型数字陷阱。  借用原文：getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about the money collected from Rome's Trevie Fountain?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about Thomas Morgan?
options: He was arrested for stealing money from four fountain cleaners.
He was sentenced to 34 years' imprisonment.
He collected rare coins from around the world.
He stole a lot of money from a fountain with a magnetic stick.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about Thomas Morgan? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于Thomas Morgan说了什么? 
 A)  他因从四名喷泉清洁工那里偷钱而被逮捕。 
 B)  他被判处34年监禁。 
 C)  他收集来自世界各地的稀有硬币。 
 D)  他用磁棒从喷泉中偷了很多钱。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） He stole a lot of money from a fountain with a magnetic stick. 
 【定位】 P3 Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick. 
 当局最终抓获一名臭名昭著、名叫 Thomas Morgan 的小偷，并禁止他靠近喷泉——此前他用一根磁棒在 34 年间钓走了数千美元的零钱。
